abstract.p: This invention relates to a tool clamping device for a machine spindle (1) wherein said tool clamping device includes a drawbar (16) at one end of the drawbar a clamping organ (18) is arranged in order to clamp part of a tool coupling at said end, plus a device to exert an axially directed force on the drawbar (16) in a direction away from the clamping device (18). The invention relates also to a machine spindle which includes a clamping unit according to this invention. The clamping device according to this invention is characterized by the fact that unit (5), in order that it should be able to exert a force on the drawbar (16), includes a housing (7), a piston (9) within the housing which can be displaced axially plus a compressible pressure medium (6) enclosed in the housing (7).

L'invention concerne un dispositif de verrouillage d'outil pour broche de machine (1), lequel comprend une barre de traction (16) à une extrémité de laquelle se trouve un organe de verrouillage (18), qui permet de verrouiller une partie de couplage d'outil à cette extrémité. Le dispositif comprend en outre un dispositif exerçant une force axiale sur la barre de traction (16) dans une direction qui s'éloigne du dispositif de verrouillage (18). L'invention concerne en outre une broche de machine qui comprend une unité de verrouillage conforme à la description. Le dispositif de verrouillage considéré est caractérisé en ce que l'unité (5), pour pouvoir exercer une force sur la barre de traction (16), comprend un boîtier (7), un piston (9) susceptible d'être déplacé axialement à l'intérieur de ce boîtier, et un milieu sous pression (6) dans l'enceinte du boîtier (7).

description.p: TOOL CLAMPING DEVICE
Technical field of the invention

This invention relates to a tool clamping device for a machine spindle, where said tool clamping device includes a drawbar, at one end of the drawbar a clamping organ is arranged in order to clamp part of a tool coupling at said end, plus a device to exert an axially directed force on the drawbar in a direction away from the clamping device.
State of the art of the technology
Reference is made to the attached Fig. A and the associated descriptive section below for a more detailed explanation of the prior art.
Objects and features of the invention
A primary object of the present invention is to present a tool clamping device for a machine spindle which is completely symmetrical and thereby, to a large degree, free from vibration.
A further object of the present invention is to present a tool clamping device which is capable of withstanding more clamping cycles than the prior art.
An additional object of the present invention is to reduce the axial length of the tool clamping device more exactly the object is to reduce the length by approximately 50%.
A further object of the present invention is that the tool clamping device should be easier to assemble in the casing of the machine spindle.

The objects of this invention have been achieved through a tool-clamping device, which incorporates the features indicated in the following patent claims. The preferred embodiments of the invention are defined in the dependent patent claims.
Brief description of the drawings
In the following, an embodiment of the invention is described with reference to the attached drawings where
Fig. A shows a longitudinal section through a machine spindle with a tool clamping device according to prior art; and
Fig. 1 shows a longitudinal section through a machine spindle in which a tool clamping device according to this invention is assembled.
Detailed description of prior art plus a preferred embodiment of the invention

Known machine spindles commonly include a tool-clamping device of the type, which is shown in the attached Fig. A. The said tool clamping device includes a drawbar B, which has a first end which is connected to a clamping bar C which is part of a tool clamping device, which in its operative position is in engagement with a part of a tool coupling (not shown), for example of the Coromant Capto® or ISO-cone type. The said clamping bar C features pivotable, secured segments D, the free ends of which are displaced radially outwards when the clamping bar C takes up its operative position. The drawbar B is actuated by a group of individual disc springs E, as shown in Fig. A, or by a helical disc spring. The drawbar B is displaced to one of its end positions within the machine spindle when the springs/spring find themselves in the expanded state. When the drawbar B finds itself in said one end position the clamping bar C will be found in its operative position, that is to say it clamps a part of the tool coupling (not illustrated) which is attached to said clamping bar C. In order to release the said (not illustrated) part of a tool coupling the drawbar B is displaced, with axial compression of the disc springs E, in the direction towards the clamping bar C. At that point the free ends of the segments D will pivot inwards and the tool coupling part (which has not been illustrated) can be removed.
A clear disadvantage with the clamping device described above is that the disc springs E exhibit a play in relationship to the drawbar B, that is to say they have a centre hole which is larger than the diameter B of the drawbar. The same applies to the centre hole of a helical disc spring. As a result of the above the said play will result in the spindle running out of true, which in turn will lead to vibration and the spindle being unbalanced, these problems being specially noticeable at high rotational speeds.

In order to generate sufficiently high clamping forces the spring must feature a large quantity of discs, respectively turns. As a result of this the spring in question, irrespective of whether it is a disc spring E or a helical disc spring, will have a considerable axial length, which in turn will lead to the length of the machine spindle similarly being of considerable length. This implies a disadvantage when handling, clamping and rotating the machine spindles.

A machine spindle of the type described above is capable of approximately 500,000 clamping cycles, whereby each cycle involves clamping and releasing of part of a tool coupling. This can appear to be a reassuring quantity but, in fact, a multiple increase in the number of clamping cycles, preferably four times, would be an exceptional advantage in this application.
The machine spindle shown in Fig. 1 includes a casing 3, inside which a clamping device according to this invention is assembled.

The clamping device, according to this invention, includes as a main component a "pulling" gas spring which is loosely attached to the inside of the housing 3. As can be seen from the upper part of Fig. 1 the gas spring 5, includes a cylindrical housing 7, which at its left hand end in Fig. 1 lies against a stop 8, in the housing 3, which thus hinders the housing 7, of the gas spring 5 from being displaced in an upwards direction according to Fig. 1. A displaceable piston 9, is provided inside the housing 7, which at its one end features a cylindrical end part 10, which lies in contact with the internal limiting endwall of the house 7, via seals 11 and 12, said seals run along the circumference of said cylindrical end part. In general the cylindrical end part 10, has a
larger diameter than the piston 9. At the end of the housing 7, which is positioned close to the end part 10, the housing 7, is provided with an abutment shoulder, which extends through 360° and inwards towards the centre of the housing 7. The cylindrical end part 10 rests against the said shoulder when it is displaced as far downwards as is possible in Fig. 1. The purpose of the seals 11 and 12 is to seal the space between the cylindrical end part 10 and the internal limiting end wall of the housing from a gas medium, which is encased in the gas spring. The piston 9, features a first centre through hole 4, for coolant.

The free end 14, of the piston 9, extends outwards through the left-hand gable in Fig. 1 of the housing 7. The said free end 14, is connected via a first threaded coupling to the drawbar 16, which features another central, through hole 17, for coolant, the purpose of which hole is to transport coolant from the under end of the drawbar 16 in Fig. 1 to its upper end in Fig. 1. The drawbar 16 is provided at its upper end in Fig. 1 with a clamping unit in the form of segment 18, said segments being held fast at one end and being pivotable towards the drawbar 16, the free ends of said segments are able to pivot radially outwards to an operating position when the drawbar is displaced downwards as shown in Fig. 1.

A radially outwards projecting flange 19, which extends all the way round the circumference is provided in a middle portion of the piston 9, whereby said flange acts as a stop when the piston 9, is displaced in a direction towards the upper end in Fig. 1 of the machine spindle. The said flange 19, will hence come into abutment against a gable element 20, of the gas spring 5, and more precisely against the under end in Fig. 1 of the said gable element 20.

As can be seen from Fig. 1 the gable element 20, is attached to the housing 7, of the gas spring 5, by a seal 21, which seals the cavity between the gable element 20, and the internal limiting wall of the housing 7, in relation to the gas medium 6, which is encased in the gas spring 5. The gable element 20, is provided with further seals 22, 23, 24, which seal the cavity between the piston 9 and the gable element 20, in relation to the gas medium 6, which is encased in the gas spring 5. Normally the pressure of the
encased gas medium 6, is approximately 150 bar. According to a practice which is preferred at present the machine spindles 1 , are delivered with the associated gas spring 5, in "uncharged" condition, that is to say without the pressurized gas medium 6. The reason for this is that gas springs of the type in question may not, according to regulations at present in force, be transported by air transport if they contain gas which has a pressure of the order of 150 bar. The gas springs 5, are normally "charged" prior to delivery to a customer, for this reason gas springs 5, are provided with a filling nipple (not shown) or something similar. The said nipple can obviously be used in situations where the gas medium is to be checked or maintained.

In the area of its free end the cylindrical end part 10, features an internal thread which together with an external thread on a push rod 25, forms a second threaded joint 26. The said push rod 25, is displaceably positioned within the casing 3, of the machine spindle and is sealed against the inner limiting wall by a seal 27. The push rod 25, features a third, central, though channel for coolant 28. The function of said push rod 25, will be explained below.

The machine spindle 1 , in Fig. 1 is shown in the situation where the piston 9, is displaced downwards to the maximum. At the same time the standing piston 9, under the pressure of the gas medium 6, has in turn displaced the drawbar 16, to the maximum downwards position and the segments 18, have taken up their operative positions, that is to say the free ends of the pivotable secured segments 18, have been displaced radially outwards to interlock with a part (not shown) of a tool coupling, for example of the COROMANT CAPTO® or ISO-cone type. Thus the encased gas medium 6, within the housing of the gas spring 5, exerts a pressure on an internal radial surface 29 of the cylindrical end part 10, which leads to the piston 9, and drawbar 16 being exposed to a permanent force acting in an axial direction which endeavours to displace this element downwards in Fig. 1. This said permanent, axially operating force ensures that the non- illustrated part of the tool coupling is reliably secured to the free end of the drawbar 16.

When the non-illustrated part of the tool coupling is to be released from the drawbar 16, the push rod 25 is displaced upwards in Fig. 1 in relation to the casing 3, of the machine
spindle. The said displacement is achieved by allowing the push rod 25, to be influenced by some suitable external organ, which is not illustrated. Hence the push rod 25, will displace the piston 9, in relation to both the housing 7, of gas spring 5, and the casing, of the machine spindle. The said displacement of the piston 9, occurs in opposition to the influence of the gas medium 6, which is encased in the gas spring 5, which is thus compressible. The piston 9, which at its free end is connected to the drawbar 16, will thus displace the said drawbar upwards in Fig. 1, whereby the non-illustrated part of the tool coupling can be released in that the free ends of the segments 18, pivot radially inwards. When the force from the push rod ceases, that is to say when the push rod 25, is caused to revert to its position in accordance with Fig. 1, the spring 9, and even the drawbar 16, will revert to the position illustrated in Fig. 1 where the drawbar 16, is not linked to any part of a tool coupling. Obviously it is possible, and even most normal, that a new part of a tool coupling is attached to the free end of the drawbar 16, immediately after the existing part of the tool coupling has been removed, that is to say the push rod 25, in its upwards displaced position in Fig. 1 during the change of a not- shown part of a tool coupling.

To summarize, therefore, it has been established that a gas spring which exerts an equivalent force to that of a disc spring or a helical disc spring has a considerably smaller axial length than said disc spring. Furthermore the gas spring does not include any loose elements which at high speeds of rotation can cause unbalance of the machine spindle and thereby subsequent vibration.
Possible modifications of the invention

In certain applications the clamping device on a machine spindle can be provided with a system of wedges which create a favourable conversion during the transfer of the forces acting on the drawbar to the clamping device on said drawbar 16. Thus this invention is not limited to only the embodiment of drawbar 16, shown in Fig. 1 but covers even clamping devices with different types of force conversion units and within the framework of the present invention are offered a number of different alternative ways
for the person skilled in the art with regard to the transfer of forces from the drawbar 16, to the clamping device.
The examples of tool couplings described above are by no means thoroughly exhaustive and clamping units on a drawbar 16, can be designed in several different ways in order to match different tools.

In the embodiment described above the unit which brings a permanent force to bear on the drawbar of a gas spring 5, in which a gas medium is encased. However one can, within the framework of the present invention, even think of other types of pressure medium which are encapsulated in housing and which influence a piston which can be displaced axially. What must however apply in this respect is that the pressure medium is compressible in order to make possible the displacement of the push rod 25, upwards in Fig. 1.

claim.claim-text: 1. Clamping device on a machine spindle (1), where said clamping device includes a drawbar (16), at one end of which is arranged a clamping unit (18) in order to clamp part of a tool coupling at the said end, plus a unit (5) to exert an axial force on the drawbar (16) in a direction away from the clamping unit (18), characterized in that the unit (5) for exerting a force on the drawbar (16) includes a housing (7), a piston in the housing which can be axially displaced plus a compressible pressure medium which is encapsulated in the housing (7).
2. Clamping device according to claim 1, characterized in, that the unit for the application of the force is in the form of a gas spring (5).

3. Clamping device according to claims lor2, characterized in, that the piston (9) in the force application unit (5) includes a cylindrical end part (10), plus units (11, 12) in order to seal the said end part (10) from the cylindrical house (7) from the compressible pressure medium (6).
4. Clamping device according to any of claims 1-3, characterized in, that the piston (9) features a free end (14), that is attached to the drawbar (16) by a threaded coupling (15).
5. Clamping device according to any of the above claims, characterized in, that the piston (9) and drawbar (16) feature central, through channels for a coolant medium (4 respectively 17).

6. Clamping device according to any of the above claims, characterized in, that the unit (5), which exerts a force features a gable unit (20), which is intended to cooperate with a flange attached to the piston (9).

7. A machine spindle (1) which includes a casing (3), in which a clamping unit plus a push rod (25) are arranged, wherein the clamping device includes a drawbar (16), at the
one end of the drawbar is arranged a clamping unit (18), in order to clamp a part of tool coupling to said end, plus unit (5) to exert an axially directed force on the drawbar in the direction away from away from the clamping unit (18), characterized in, that the unit (5), which exerts an axially directed force on the drawbar (16), includes a housing (7), a piston (9), which can be displaced axially within the housing plus a compressible pressure medium (6) which is encapsuled in the housing (7).

8. A machine spindle (1) according to claim 7, characterized in, that the unit for exerting a force in a direction away from the clamping unit (18) on the drawbar (16) consists of a gas spring (5), which includes a cylindrical housing (7), a piston (9) which can be moved axially which in turn comprises a cylindrical end part (10), plus units (11, 12) which seal the end part (10) against the housing (7) in relation to the compressible pressure medium (6).

9. A machine spindle (1) according to claim 8, characterized in, that the piston (9) features a free end (14), which is connected to the drawbar (16) via a first threaded coupling (15), and that the push bar (25) is connected to the piston (9) via a second threaded coupling.
10. A machine spindle (1) according to any of claims 7-9, characterized in, that the drawbar (16), the piston (9) plus the push bar (25) all feature through channels for coolant (17, 4, 28).
